name: Automate the Schwab RPS ingest (schwab/silver/rps has no automated producer -- it is a human running two scripts against Andrew's OneDrive)
description:
Registered 2026-07-09 by 2.0.0_SA_COO at CTO's direction (1.0.0_SA_CTO 214528Z). DEFERRED BY ANDREW'S OWN ORDERING -- explicitly sequenced AFTER Inflection. Do not start.

THE FINDING: `s3://opal-data-bd/schwab/silver/rps/` last partition = `date=20260706`, written 2026-07-07T10:44:43Z. Nothing since. `sync_schwab_onedrive_to_s3.py` documents the mechanism in its own docstring: the Schwab SI2 Desktop client delivers per-account CRS*.{ext} files to a locally-configured Destination folder; the canonical 49F location is `C:\Users\AndrewBerman\OneDrive - Opal Capital\Documents\Schwab Data Delivery\08242234\`. Usage is `python sync_schwab_onedrive_to_s3.py --upload` and THEN `convert_schwab_rps_to_parquet.py`. A human runs both.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the root cause of the MDPF Inflection-AUM freeze. MDPF's convergence gate is AND-composed, so a stale 49F custody feed defers the whole chain -- Inflection itself is fresh every day (the gate's own log: `inflection: fresh=true, as_of=2026-07-09`). Andrew, verbatim: "49 Financial should not hold up MDPF, that is nonsensical." The contract agrees (SS3.5-decision-iv adopted per-partner roll-forward); the gate is stricter than the contract it implements.

AND THE GATE FIX ALONE IS NOT SAFE. 49F's `non_model_aua` is a RESIDUAL whose minuend (RPS custody) is frozen while its subtrahends stay fresh. Un-gating alone resumes that corruption daily instead of never; the deferred chain is the only thing currently holding it still (NEVER#6 logic applied to a data path). Hence the 0.6.0 per-partner-gate + 0.4.0 WS-E-guard CO-ACTIVATION: neither lands alone.

THE IDENTITY -- TWO ARTIFACTS, TWO CORRECT FORMS. DO NOT "RECONCILE" THEM. This row briefly carried a claim that CTO's arithmetic was off by a term; 0.6.0 raised it (215706Z) and then RETRACTED IT ITSELF (220011Z) before it was committed. Both figures are exact; they measure DIFFERENT FIELDS:

  SERVED field    d(non_model) = d(custody) - d(model)               <- CTO. `model_aua` fell $10,474,162.28;
                                                                        the served plug rose by exactly that.
  FEEDER field    d(non_model) = d(custody) - d(model) - d(sma)      <- 0.6.0, on mdpf/feeds/.../49financial/:
                    d(custody) = +0.00 (frozen to the cent) | d(model) = -10,474,162.28 | d(sma) = +93,737.35
                    d(non_model) = +10,380,424.93

The $93,737.35 is the drift of a term the SERVED field does not contain. 0.6.0's rule, from its own retraction: "never publish a delta without the operands that produced it -- I only escaped because I showed the four columns; had I shown the difference alone, CTO would have accepted a false correction."

What survives, and it is the load-bearing part: 0.4.0_DS and 0.6.0 independently reach the same design conclusion -- the alignment guard must bind THREE operands to one as-of, not two. `sma_aua_input` is a full term. A two-operand guard leaves it free and the residual absorbs it silently.

BLAST RADIUS: **UNDETERMINED, pending `partner_custody_as_of` (contract SS4) or a build-time reconstruction.** NOT 3 days, NOT 8 rows, NOT 6. 0.6.0 first reported "6 rows / 3 episodes" and RETRACTED IT (220011Z): it had labelled an INFERRED selector as a measured "custody TRUE vintage." There IS no custody vintage field on the row (DS established this) -- `as_of_date` belongs to the SUBTRAHEND. Source settles the minuend: `build_mdpf_wse_49f_non_model_aua.py:762` -> `rps_date = args.rps_date or _latest_rps_partition()`, i.e. whatever RPS's newest partition was AT BUILD TIME -- a wall-clock property of the build, NOT a function of `as_of`. It is neither `max(RPS <= as_of)` (0.6.0's inference) nor `max(RPS cap WSB)` (the proposed fix).

A selector-independent re-run over artifact values alone (custody unchanged while a subtrahend moved) yields 8 rows -- 2026-05-19, 05-27, 06-10, 06-15, 06-22, 06-23, 07-07, 07-08 -- overlapping the retracted 6 on ONLY 07-07 and 07-08, the two days already known. **Two methods, two answers, agreement only where it did not matter.** The 06-13/14 weekend rows (d_model = d_sma = +0.00) are correctly unflagged by BOTH methods: the positive control on the discriminator, and the one thing the two runs agree on.

**DS's `partner_custody_as_of` is not merely a precondition for the GUARD -- it is a precondition for the CENSUS. You cannot count the damage until the field exists.** That is a stronger argument for the schema change than any census would have been. RECOVERABLE, not in-window: each feeder row carries `_ingested_at`; reconstruct `_latest_rps_partition()` as of that instant from the RPS partitions' own `LastModified` and the true minuend vintage falls out per row, with no assumption. (DS: "when the artifact cannot answer, the producer's inputs still exist.") CTO's call on who runs it after 02:00Z.

SEPARATE FINDING, DO NOT FOLD INTO THE RESIDUAL FIX (CTO 215559Z): served `non_model_aua` = feeder `non_model_aua` + `sma_aua`, established to the cent on three dates; there is no partner-level `sma_aua` field in the served file at all. Contract AMENDMENT 1 (Andrew-direct, 2026-05-18) requires 1a and 1c be "separately tracked and separately reported ... never a combined figure." The FEEDER complies; the AGGREGATION layer folds $23.47M of SMA into "non-model" on the served page. The arithmetic identity holds; the CLASSIFICATION does not. Open against `mdpf_aggregate_aua.py` as its own finding -- if it rides in on the residual change, nobody reviews it against the contract it violates.

CAVEAT, CARRIED AS THE ROW'S OWN TEXT AND BINDING ON WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP (CTO, verbatim, flagging his own negative): "`aws events list-rules` surfaces only `canonical-schwab-si2-download-schedule` (a different tree), and `comp-grep` over `infra/` finds no Lambda writer. CAVEAT, and hold me to it: that negative is a claim about my query -- I matched EventBridge rule *names* on `rps`/`schwab`. A rule named otherwise would not have surfaced. STRONGLY SUPPORTED, not proven. Have someone confirm before anyone writes 'there is no producer' in a doc."

NOBODY WRITES "there is no automated producer" AS FACT until that confirmation lands. Rule 22: a causal claim is a HYPOTHESIS until source/graph-confirmed; "proof / provably / root cause / definitively" are reserved words. The FIRST deliverable of this project is the confirming read (dataflow/graph, not a name-matched grep), not the automation.

SETTLED AND NOT TO BE RE-OPENED: the 06-26 -> 07-01 six-day MDPF hole is NOT this. CTO initially attributed it to the same manual feed, then retracted himself within 20 minutes, before any dispatch: RPS wrote on 06-26, 06-29, 06-30, 07-01 and 07-02 -- every trading day across the hole -- and the RPS repoint did not land until 2026-07-01T21:14:05Z, AFTER it. Throughout that hole the gate was keyed on `silver/{allocations,fees}` and had never heard of RPS; a feed the gate was not reading cannot have caused a defer. 0.5.0_AE_OpalETL's `silver/fees` attribution STANDS on its own evidence. Two silences separated by a repoint. Distinct cause, distinct window, distinct gate configuration.

DELIVERABLE 1 WAS COMPLETED BEFORE THE CANCELLATION LANDED, and its result is recorded here so nobody re-runs it. 0.5.0_AE_OpalETL (223943Z) upgraded the negative from CTO's STRONGLY-SUPPORTED to **ESTABLISHED**: nothing on an automated trigger (EventBridge Rule, EventBridge Scheduler, S3-event, or Step Function) writes opal-data-bd/schwab/silver/rps/. Proven by TARGET ARN, never by name, across FIVE surfaces with every denominator stated and cross-checked:
  (1) EventBridge RULES 131/131, denominator cross-checked TWO ways (name-array count == manual-pagination sum; `length(Rules)` would have under-counted at 100+31). 139 target ARNs. The 2 schwab-named targets drive the CANONICAL pipeline and their EC2 roles are explicitDeny on opal-data-bd/* -- FIRM-SEPARATION is what excludes them.
  (2) EventBridge SCHEDULER 7/7 by ARN -- a DISTINCT API that `list-rules` does not see; checking it closed a silent gap.
  (3) S3 event notifications on opal-data-bd: 3 triggers, none on any schwab prefix.
  (4) Step Functions: 0 matching.
  (5) IAM PutObject reach on the prefix (the strong, name-independent form): 180/180 roles + 5/5 IAMUsers, 0 errors. 8 roles allowed, ALL bd-pipeline; users only Andrew_Berman{,_1} (the human path). None is a scheduled schwab-RPS converter -- they can write the prefix because they hold broad opal-data-bd/* write, not because anything schedules them.
0.5.0 avoided both of 0.4.0_DS's traps (for-loop over an array, not `while read`; every `aws` call `</dev/null`; batched past the 2-min timeout).

WHAT THE SWEEP WOULD NOT HAVE SURFACED (0.5.0's own boundary, stated unprompted): a principal/rule/schedule/notification/SFN created after its ~2026-07-09T22:2xZ snapshot; a cross-region scheduler in another region driving one of the 8 roles (it enumerated us-east-1 only, where the bucket lives); a writer that ASSUMES one of the 8 roles from outside. And CloudTrail CANNOT corroborate from the write side -- the org trail is ReadOnly on opal-data-bd and served-key-write-trail covers platinum/firm/ only, so a PutObject to schwab/silver/rps is forensically invisible and there is no observed-write oracle for this prefix without enabling data events.

The manual producer is bd-exporter-ec2-role via the agent/human-invoked /49-schwab-conv path, and NO EventBridge rule starts or commands that EC2. The automation gap was real and proven. It is now moot.
